claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase solid solution.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has low to intermediate stacking-fault energy.
Low to intermediate stacking-fault energy promotes twin formation during deformation.
Low to intermediate stacking-fault energy promotes cross-slip during deformation.
Twin formation and cross-slip improve the alloy's ductility and machinability by providing alternative deformation routes.
Twin formation and cross-slip reduce dislocation pile-up and work hardening.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and work hardening cause lower hardness and strength.
CoCrFeNiTi with low stacking-fault energy has lower hardness and strength than otherwise comparable alloys with higher stacking-fault energy.
Dislocation-core structures, stacking-fault widths, and twin formation can serve as experimental proxies for effective stacking-fault energy.
The as-cast starting alloy exhibits favorable ductility and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
The starting alloy should show pronounced twin formation and cross-slip during in-situ TEM deformation.
The starting alloy should show only a low increment in work hardening and hardness during deformation.
Raising stacking-fault energy should increase dislocation immobilization and pile-up.
Raising stacking-fault energy should reduce twin activity and cross-slip activity.
Raising stacking-fault energy should measurably increase hardness and yield strength.
The proposed mechanism applies up to 400 °C under moderate strain rates, provided the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without significant microstructural evolution.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, but the proposed controlled intervention includes an unspecified compositional tweak, which would produce a non-equimolar alloy unless explicitly designed otherwise.
